account: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof (reinforcement learning over the Lean proof language) and AlphaGeometry 2 produced solutions to four of the six 2024 International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) problems. Because the systems work in formal language, the problems were first translated manually. One problem was solved within minutes and others took up to three days, longer than the contest allows. Two former IMO gold medalists, Sir Timothy Gowers and Joseph Myers, graded the solutions under IMO rules. They awarded 28 of 42 points, a silver-medal score. DeepMind announced the result on 25 July 2024 and did not give the grading date. In July 2025 a Gemini Deep Think model working in natural language within the time limit scored 35 of 42. IMO president Gregor Dolinar confirmed this as a gold-medal score. Nature reported that OpenAI also claimed a gold-level result. DeepMind's AlphaProof team published the peer-reviewed account of the IMO 2024 run in Nature on 12 November 2025. The authors report that experts formalized the five non-geometry problems in Lean right after the problems were released and that the Lean kernel verified each AlphaProof proof. They state that the 28 points fell one point below the gold-medal threshold of 29, which 58 of 609 contestants reached.

ai_role.statement: The AI systems produced the proofs. Humans manually formalized the 2024 problem statements into Lean (Scientific American) and graded the output. In 2024 the solutions were graded by two mathematicians at DeepMind's request (one of them, Myers, chaired the IMO 2024 Problem Selection Committee). The result was not officially certified by the IMO. DeepMind states the 2025 result was graded and certified by IMO coordinators, with the IMO president's confirmation appearing in the vendor blog. The cited sources do not state whether OpenAI's 2025 claim was certified by the IMO.

fields.account: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof (reinforcement learning over the Lean proof language) and AlphaGeometry 2 produced solutions to four of the six 2024 International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) problems. Because the systems work in formal language, the problems were first translated manually. One problem was solved within minutes and others took up to three days, longer than the contest allows. Two former IMO gold medalists, Sir Timothy Gowers and Joseph Myers, graded the solutions under IMO rules. They awarded 28 of 42 points, a silver-medal score. DeepMind announced the result on 25 July 2024 and did not give the grading date. In July 2025 a Gemini Deep Think model working in natural language within the time limit scored 35 of 42. IMO president Gregor Dolinar confirmed this as a gold-medal score. Nature reported that OpenAI also claimed a gold-level result. DeepMind's AlphaProof team published the peer-reviewed account of the IMO 2024 run in Nature on 12 November 2025. The authors report that experts formalized the five non-geometry problems in Lean right after the problems were released and that the Lean kernel verified each AlphaProof proof. They state that the 28 points fell one point below the gold-medal threshold of 29, which 58 of 609 contestants reached.
